cards.hearing: You may be hearing that stocks just hit a fresh record high today, with a lot of excitement around AI-related chip companies.
cards.why: Record highs often come with a wave of good feeling, and that can make everyday life feel a little more comfortable, from spending to planning ahead.
cards.but: But one great day is still just one day, and it does not rewrite a long-term plan.
cards.story: Picture a runner who hits a personal best on a Tuesday morning jog. It is a great morning, but the training plan does not change because of one fast mile.
say: We celebrate the good day and keep the plan exactly as it is.
One record session is a nice moment, not a new strategy.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing that the President is considering pausing the federal gas tax to help with costs at the pump.
cards.why: Lower fuel costs can mean cheaper trucking, which can nudge down the price of groceries and everyday goods.
cards.but: But this is just talk of a possible policy right now, not something that changes your long-term plan today.
cards.story: Think of it like hearing a store might run a sale next month. You don't rearrange your whole budget around a maybe. You wait and see what actually happens.
say: We don't plan around maybes. We plan around what's actually happened.
If it happens, we'll talk about what it means. For now, nothing changes.

cards.hearing: You may be hearing that the political map for the Senate is shifting, with a once-safe state now considered up for grabs.
cards.why: Election season brings a lot of noise, and people naturally wonder if a different Congress means different rules for their money.
cards.but: But markets have moved through every kind of political mix before, and your plan isn't built around one election outcome.
cards.story: Picture choosing a sturdy car for a long road trip, not because you know every turn in the road ahead, but because you trust the car to handle whatever comes. Elections are just more turns in the road.
say: Your plan isn't betting on one party or one race.
We built this for the long road, not for one election night.
